findings.summary: The shared revoke operation now requires owner reauthentication, but Block also invokes this operation, and neither the Block affordance nor the block journey includes any reauthentication.
findings.evidence: operation.connection.revoke: "preconditions: [Participant authority, Owner reauthentication]"; affordance.ConnectionPanel.block: "trigger: Owner confirms Block", "preconditions: [Contact is linked to an Account]"; J.control.block b2: "Choose Block and confirm" -> b3 operation.connection.revoke

findings.summary: The disconnect journey now asks the user to reauthenticate, but it has no reauthentication check or failure branch; the only outcomes are confirm or cancel, unlike the export and delete journeys.
findings.evidence: d2: "Choose Disconnect, confirm and reauthenticate" next: [d3 when confirm, e2 when cancel]; affordance failure: "Reauthentication failure denies the disconnect"; compare J.control.delete z3 "Owner reauthentication checked" -> f1 "when: reauthentication failed"

findings.summary: The criterion now claims that disconnect without fresh reauthentication is denied, but its only hook's fixture still covers just revoke-after-queue and retry, so the new obligation has no executable evidence.
findings.evidence: claim: "... Disconnect without fresh reauthentication is denied"; hook.webapp.revocation.current inputs: fixture: "revoke after queue, retry dispatch and access"
